items.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: Roswell and I and the saxophone player got X’d and they have never had horns since then.

ctx.x: Do you get a chance to play much these days?

No. Very, very little. I worked the hotels and this you didn’t know and now you will know, I worked here, because of a couple of reasons. A good friend of mine and a wonderful saxophone player, Milty Hisler was working here. And the band played a show, that’s all, except for a dance set at the end and maybe a couple of tunes at the end. But that was the reason I got started over here. Then one Labor Day the leader came down from Charles Slesky’s office, who owns all this stuff, and he said, “No more horns.” Well…
